title: Field Enablement Email + LMS Outline — Redwood Standard Demo v1 (Draft)

body:
WORKING DOC (draft). Goal: send rollout comms to AEs/SEs and publish an LMS module so the Standard Demo v1 is run consistently (and without surprise breakage).

Owner: Renee Sullivan (Enablement)
Exec sponsor: Jordan Blake (CRO)
Demo program owner: Markus Klein (Dir. Solutions Engineering)
Deck/talk track lead: Soojin Lee (PMM)

============================================================
1) FIELD ROLLOUT EMAIL (DRAFT)
============================================================

Subject options (pick one):
A) Now Live: Redwood Standard Demo v1 + Demo Tenant (Training Required)
B) New: Stable “Standard Demo v1” + resettable demo tenant — how to access + what to run
C) Standard Demo v1 rollout: talk track, deck, scenarios, and support path

To: All AEs + SEs
CC: Sales leadership (Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer), PMM (Soojin Lee), SE leadership (Markus Klein)
From: Field Enablement (Renee Sullivan) + Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein)

———

Hi team,

We’re rolling out Redwood Standard Demo v1: a reliable, repeatable demo tenant + a scripted talk track + a standard deck.

Why this matters:
- Fewer “hero” demos: stable setup and fast reset with known-good scenarios.
- Cleaner narrative: shows Redwood’s differentiators (latency/cost controls, reliability/fallback, deployment flexibility, observability).
- Safer in front of prospects: sanitized tenant, no sensitive data, and an explicit Plan B for live failure modes.

What’s included in Standard Demo v1:
1) Standard Demo Deck v1 (slides + persona emphasis)
2) Master talk track script (with timing + persona branches)
3) Known-good scenario set (scripted inputs + expected outputs + fallback steps)
4) Demo tenant reset checklist (pre/post demo)
5) Security FAQ for demo calls (retention/logging/encryption/SSO posture + how the demo tenant is isolated)

What changed (vs. “whatever we demoed last time”):
- Model versions are pinned per scenario to reduce output drift.
- Routing + fallback is pre-configured in the demo tenant (we show it live; no ad-hoc edits during calls).
- Quotas/rate limits are set to demo-safe defaults to avoid mid-call throttling surprises.
- Prebuilt Console dashboards/saved views are included and used as part of the talk track.

Where to find the assets (single source of truth):
- Talk track (speaker notes): [LINK] “Talk Track - Redwood Standard Demo (Speaker Notes)”
- Deck: [LINK] “Deck - Redwood Standard Demo (Working)” (use the ‘Latest’ version in the doc header)
- Demo tenant setup/runbook: [LINK] Confluence: Demo tenant setup runbook
- Demo tenant reset checklist: [LINK] Drive: Demo Tenant Reset Checklist
- Security FAQ (for security/procurement persona): [LINK] Confluence: Demo Tenant Security FAQ

How to access the demo tenant (IMPORTANT):
- Access is provisioned via RBAC group. Do not share accounts or API keys.
- Request access using: [LINK] “Demo Tenant Access Request” form (or follow the instructions in the runbook).
- After approval, you’ll be assigned:
  - Console access to the demo tenant
  - A demo API key (scoped, demo-only) if needed for scripted scenarios
- If you are presenting in EMEA and need EU-only routing/data residency narrative, flag it in the request form (we’ll assign the correct region config).

Required training (15–25 minutes total):
- Before using Standard Demo v1 with a prospect, you must complete the LMS module:
  - “Running the Redwood Standard Demo v1”
  - Includes: scenario run order, what to click in Console, how to narrate variability, and Plan B steps.
- Certification: pass the short knowledge check (8–10 questions). This unlocks ‘Presenter’ permissions.

When to use the demo tenant vs. a prospect-specific trial:
- Use the demo tenant when you want a fast, safe, consistent story OR you need to showcase routing/fallback + cost/latency dashboards without setup time.
- Use a prospect-specific trial when you need to run their prompts/data (following the approved process), integrate with their systems, or validate workload-specific performance.
- CRM guidance: log “Standard Demo v1” under activity type = Demo (Standard) for consistent reporting.

Support path (please follow this so we can keep reliability high):
- If something breaks during prep or live:
  1) Follow the “Plan B” steps in the scenario script (usually: switch to canned output / switch scenario / show dashboard screenshot).
  2) File an issue:
     - P0 (demo happening now): post in #demo-tenant-help with: region, scenario, timestamp, screenshot, error text
     - P1/P2 (not live): open Jira ticket (Project: INT-SUPPORT) with labels: demo-tenant, standard-demo-v1
  3) If you need immediate help within business hours, tag @DemoTenant-Oncall in Slack (#demo-tenant-help)

Next enablement sessions:
- Live 30-min walkthrough + Q&A (run by SE + PMM):
  - NA session: [DATE/TIME + CAL LINK]
  - EMEA session: [DATE/TIME + CAL LINK]

Thank you for helping us make demos consistent and high-signal.

— Renee (Field Enablement) + Markus (Solutions Engineering)

============================================================
2) LMS OUTLINE — “RUNNING THE REDWOOD STANDARD DEMO v1”
============================================================

LMS Course Title:
Running the Redwood Standard Demo v1 (Hosted → Dedicated → Private paths)

Audience:
- Required: Solutions Engineers, AEs who run technical demos solo
- Optional: AEs who want a tighter talk track and objection handling

Prerequisites:
- Access to demo tenant (Console)
- Basic familiarity with Redwood API (chat/completions + streaming)

Time to complete:
15–25 minutes (self-paced)

Learning objectives:
1) Run the 4–6 known-good scenarios end-to-end without making on-the-fly tenant changes.
2) Navigate Console clickpaths required for the talk track (routes, rollouts, dashboards, error analysis).
3) Explain routing/fallback behavior accurately (what we show vs. what we claim).
4) Handle common objections (latency/cost, reliability, security posture, deployment modes) using approved language.
5) Execute Plan B steps if a scenario fails or output varies.

Course structure:

Module 0 — Orientation (2 min)
- What Standard Demo v1 is (and isn’t)
- What “demo tenant” means (sanitized, stable configs, no customer data)
- The 3 primary personas and how the narrative shifts:
  - Platform Eng: reliability, routing, operational control
  - ML Eng: model choice, quality controls, evals
  - Security/Procurement: isolation, logging/retention, encryption, SSO/RBAC

Module 1 — Getting set up (3–5 min)
- How to request access (RBAC group) + expected lead time
- Console login + selecting correct region/tenant
- Where assets live (deck, talk track, checklist, security FAQ)
- “Do not do” list:
  - Do not paste prospect data into demo tenant
  - Do not change routing policies live without approval
  - Do not share API keys/screenshots containing secrets

Module 2 — Known-good scenario walkthroughs (10–12 min)
Note: the LMS should follow the standard run order but call out allowed branching.

Scenario A: 2-minute Hosted mini-demo (streaming chat)
- Purpose: immediate value + low setup
- What to say: consistent performance + streaming + simple API
- What to show: streaming response in curl/SDK; Console latency panel
- Plan B: canned output snippet + dashboard screenshot

Scenario B: Cost/latency controls (batching/caching narrative + token cost breakdown)
- Purpose: “serving is the advantage” / unit economics
- What to show: per-route/model dashboard with token-level breakdown
- What not to promise: exact $ numbers; use approved ranges only

Scenario C: Reliability + fallback routing (core differentiator)
- Purpose: keep apps online; graceful degradation
- What to show live:
  - Route policy + fallback model/region
  - Example of capacity constraint leading to fallback (simulated)
- Plan B: pre-captured screenshot sequence + explain “what would happen”

Scenario D: Rollouts / version pinning (canary + safe updates)
- Purpose: controlled changes; reproducibility in production
- What to show: pinned model version + rollout screen + simple canary toggle

Scenario E (optional / security persona): Private/VPC + audit logs narrative
- Purpose: regulated workloads and security expectations
- What to show: architecture slide(s) + security FAQ highlights
- Strict guidance: what we can say publicly vs. “under NDA / in security package”

Module 3 — Persona branching + transitions (3–4 min)
- Platform Eng opener: routing/fallback + dashboards first
- ML Eng opener: model catalog + optimization controls + eval hooks
- Security opener: isolation/retention/encryption + how Private works
- “Pivot lines” to move from Hosted to Dedicated/Private (approved phrases)

Module 4 — Objections + approved responses (3–5 min)
Include short audio/text snippets with the exact recommended language.
- “How do you compare to [cloud provider / LLM API provider]?”
- “What happens when the model is slow/unavailable?”
- “Is output deterministic?” (how to narrate variability + why we pin versions)
- “What’s your data retention / logging posture?” (demo tenant vs. production)
- “Can you support data residency / EU-only?”
- “Can we run in our VPC/on-prem?”

Module 5 — Operations: pre-demo checks + Plan B + issue filing (3–4 min)
- Pre-demo checklist (dashboards green, quota sanity, model pinned, scripts run once)
- During demo: how to recognize trouble early (latency spikes, throttles, streaming disconnect)
- Plan B menu:
  - Switch to canned output
  - Switch scenario order
  - Use screenshots for Console views
  - Pivot to architecture/security deck section
- Where to file issues + what info to include

Knowledge check (required; 8–10 questions)
Sample question bank:
1) Which assets are the source of truth for Standard Demo v1?
2) What is the correct support path for a P0 issue during a live demo?
3) True/False: It’s acceptable to change routing policies live during a prospect demo.
4) Which scenario is recommended as the 2-minute Hosted mini-demo opener?
5) What do we say when asked for exact pricing numbers during the demo?
6) What’s the approved approach to output variability?
7) Which persona typically wants to see audit logs / retention posture first?
8) What triggers “use demo tenant” vs “spin up prospect-specific trial”?

Certification / completion criteria:
- LMS module completed + >= 80% on knowledge check
- Optional: submit a 2-minute Loom of Scenario A (streaming) + Console latency panel for review (SE managers can spot-check)

Rollout plan (internal)
- Week 1: announce + publish LMS; run 2 live training sessions (NA/EMEA)
- Week 2: office hours (2x), track completion, follow up with non-completers
- Week 3+: require certification for new SEs/AEs as part of onboarding

Open questions / TODO (for Renee)
- Confirm Slack channel name for support (proposed: #demo-tenant-help)
- Confirm Jira project/keying for internal issues (proposed: INT-SUPPORT)
- Confirm RBAC gating behavior (“Presenter” permission unlock)
- Confirm whether we need a separate EMEA/EU-only tenant selection flow in LMS screenshots
- Get final approvals on “what changed” bullets from Product (Nikhil/Marissa) + SRE (Sean/Rafael)
